title: Loading and Storing Two Words in Memory
description: Load the addresses of val1 and val2 into $t0 and $t1, read their words into $t2 and $t3, and write them back to the opposite addresses.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: In `main`, `la $t0, val1` and `la $t1, val2` load the memory addresses of `val1` and `val2`. Then `lw $t2, 0($t0)` and `lw $t3, 0($t1)` load the words stored at those addresses into `$t2` and `$t3`.

`sw $t2, 0($t1)` stores `$t2` at the address in `$t1`, `sw $t3, 0($t0)` stores `$t3` at the address in `$t0`, and lines 15-16 exit with syscall 10. `.data` initializes `val1: .word 5` and `val2: .word 6`.
Compare the base registers in the loads and stores: `$t2` is loaded from `0($t0)` and stored to `0($t1)`, while `$t3` is loaded from `0($t1)` and stored to `0($t0)`.

steps.question: After lines 11 and 12 finish, what word values are stored in memory at `val1` (`0($t0)`) and `val2` (`0($t1)`)?

steps.description: After lines 8 and 9, `$t2` holds `5` (loaded from `val1`) and `$t3` holds `6` (loaded from `val2`).
Line 11 writes `5` to `0($t1)` (`val2`) and line 12 writes `6` to `0($t0)` (`val1`).
